hypothesis: Changing the input tile from 128 to 4096 elements while retaining the 128-thread shared-memory reduction tree and int64 accumulation may cut the large case from 32,768 initial partials to 1,024, enabling input reduction plus direct finalization in two kernels. For larger valid inputs, bounded parallel stages remain in place. This tests whether fewer CTAs and launches improve the full call despite more per-thread accumulation; it is not an assumed speedup.
notes: The catalog contains two distinct valid T1 programs: d35c915c07694ddb averaged 4.42078e-05 s, and 3eec74c802984c84 averaged 4.42746e-05 s; both were correct on the reported cases. The latter changed the finalizer cap from 1024 to 256 and was slightly slower in its three reported samples. These full-call results do not identify the cause. This candidate contrasts their 128-element input tile with a bounded 4096-element tile; correctness and repeated performance remain for controller evaluation.
transformations: Kept the 128-thread modulo/shared-memory reduction tree for input tiles, intermediate stages, and finalization.
Raised the input and intermediate reduction tile to a fixed 4096 elements; each thread accumulates its strided values in int64.
Use a bounded one-CTA direct path only for inputs no larger than one tile; larger inputs first write int64 partials to scratch.
Finalize up to 1024 partials directly to out; recursively reduce larger partial arrays in parallel stages using a second scratch buffer.
Handle n == 0 with a zero-writing kernel and reject negative n or required null pointers without reading uninitialized scratch.
